skill.name: project-research
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through scoped project research, source selection, attribution, synthesis, and reusable research patterns.
skill.summary: Guides project research with scoped questions, source tracking, citations, and synthesis.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline code formatting in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe command execution was found in the reviewed file.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 78 opens a Markdown example code fence with ```markdown. It is documentation formatting, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 83 closes the same Markdown example code fence. There is no executable command, interpolation, or instruction to run shell code.
Line 88 uses inline Markdown backticks around a local path reference. It documents integration with research subagents and does not execute commands.

content.value_statement: Research tasks often lose scope, citations, and source quality. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable research workflow.
actual_capabilities: Defines research questions, sub-questions, boundaries, and required source types.
Guides source selection across web, documentation, and academic sources.
Records confidence levels and citations for each consulted source.
Synthesizes findings into summaries with consensus, disagreements, and attribution.
Supports coordination with research subagents when available.
Provides placeholders for project-specific sources, vocabulary, and quality criteria.
limitations: It is a template and needs project-specific approved sources before production use.
It does not fetch sources by itself without tool access from the host assistant.
It does not validate citation accuracy beyond the assistant's research process.
It does not include domain-specific patterns until the user adds them.

use_cases.title: Prepare Technical Research
use_cases.description: A developer uses the workflow to compare libraries, collect documentation, and summarize tradeoffs with citations.

use_cases.title: Build Product Briefs
use_cases.description: A product manager scopes market or feature research and receives a concise synthesis with confidence notes.

use_cases.title: Maintain Knowledge Bases
use_cases.description: A documentation lead standardizes how assistants gather sources and convert findings into project guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Scope a Research Question
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-research skill to define the main question, related sub-questions, boundaries, and required source types for this topic: [topic].

prompt_templates.title: Collect Verified Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-research workflow to research [topic]. Consult up to [number] sources, note confidence for each source, and include citations.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Conflicting Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [topic] and synthesize areas of agreement, disagreement, evidence quality, and open questions. Use a comprehensive style with citations.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Research Subtasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a research effort for [topic] using available research subagents. Divide the work by source type, then synthesize results with attribution and confidence levels.

output_examples.input: Research whether our project should adopt a new search indexing library.
output_examples.output: A scoped brief with source categories, key findings, tradeoffs, confidence notes, and cited documentation links.

output_examples.input: Compare three approaches for improving onboarding documentation.
output: A summary of common guidance across sources.
A list of disagreements or weak evidence.

output_examples.input: Create reusable research patterns for this repository.
output_examples.output: A project-specific pattern section that lists triggers, recommended actions, output formats, and quality criteria.

best_practices: Replace placeholder source lists with approved project sources before regular use.
Ask the assistant to separate facts, inferences, and recommendations.
Review citations and confidence notes before sharing research externally.
anti_patterns: Do not accept claims that lack source citations or confidence notes.
Do not use the template without defining the research boundary.
Do not treat generated synthesis as final expert review for regulated decisions.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps assistants structure project research, select sources, track citations, and synthesize findings.

faq.question: Does it perform web searches automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the assistant, but searches depend on the tools available in Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.

faq.question: Can I customize the source list?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes placeholders for approved sources, domain vocabulary, output templates, and quality criteria.

faq.question: Is it useful for technical documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can standardize how documentation research is scoped, cited, and summarized.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertainty?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to record confidence levels and highlight disagreements across sources.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
